title: Authoring and support
Authoring and support
Authoring and support
text:
What the adapter checks







Supported here
Scope




Source
Moodle STACK XML <quiz> with named STACK questions; category and description entries are skipped.


Inputs
Scalar algebraic and numerical text answers, with strict syntax and <insertstars>0</insertstars> or <insertstars>1</insertstars>. Mode 0 requires *; mode 1 also accepts adjacent 2x, 2(x+1), (x+1)(x-1), and (x+1)x. Both keep xy as one symbol; whitespace alone never means multiplication. Other insertstars modes fail at import.


Variables
A small, safely parsed Maxima-like assignment and arithmetic subset, including rand(n) for seeded variants.


Tests
AlgEquiv, EqualComAss, NumAbsolute, NumRelative, NumDecPlaces; blank absolute/relative tolerances default to 0.05, while decimal places require an explicit count from 1 to 50. See the README for the expression whitelist.


PRTs
Acyclic node graphs with =, +, and − score operations, weighted response trees, branch feedback and notes.


Author tests
Native <qtest> inputs and expected PRT score, penalty, and answer note.



This is a deliberately limited evaluator, not a replacement for Moodle STACK or its Maxima CAS. questionsimplify=0 is accepted when any EqualComAss teacher form can be preserved after freezing author variables; otherwise the build rejects it. EqualComAss requires a direct input name in sans to preserve the student’s written form. Build-time validation rejects unsupported author features rather than silently grading them differently. Symbolic equivalence uses SymPy transformations rather than randomized substitution. Decimal-place grading reads the literal answer so a trailing zero is meaningful. The review interface and qtests help an author inspect parity, but they do not establish complete parity with all STACK configurations.

title: Authoring and support
text:
Validate and publish
For an extension-only installation, install sympy==1.13.3 in the Python environment used by Quarto. Run python -m stack_sympy.cli test --file questions/polynomial-expansion.xml after placing _extensions/stack-sympy on PYTHONPATH, then render with quarto render. Serve the _site directory through an HTTP server, including locally: python -m http.server --directory _site 8000. Browser grading loads Pyodide and SymPy; its first use downloads runtime packages, so it needs network access. Review the generated question and run its qtests before publishing any assessment. If a source uses features outside the supported subset, #| diagnostics: true displays the location of a build error in the page during authoring; remove it for production so unsupported questions fail the render.

title: Question corpus
text:
These are 30 native STACK XML questions from the upstream library. Each question below has a local XML download, its pinned upstream source, and a result from the current adapter. Only the six questions whose authored tests passed on all three replayed seeds have interactive cards. The others remain available for inspection, with the observed mismatch or unsupported feature shown explicitly.
The reproducible baseline reports 6 passed, 6 with test mismatches, and 18 blocked (11 at import, 7 at instantiation). It retained 73 authored test cases and replayed 72 seed/case combinations across 12 instantiated questions; 27 combinations disagreed. Passing those bounded checks is evidence for the listed seeds, not complete STACK/Maxima parity.
Attribution and reuse. Questions are from STACK / maths/moodle-qtype_stack, pinned at commit 10d323311b7f39fb7b092dd10ce75f7d8632f525. The unchanged question exports carry the CC BY-SA 4.0 license, also included locally; see each pinned source link below. The manifest records the exact upstream path and SHA-256 for every XML file.

title: Try a STACK question on a static page
text: STACK SymPy reads an ordinary Moodle STACK XML export at build time. The Quarto page contains an interactive question card; a browser worker uses the same bounded Python question model to check each response. No Moodle session is needed to try these examples. The review buttons here show the authored question tests and their expected PRT outcomes.

title: Try a STACK question on a static page
Try a STACK question on a static page
section: How to use it in your own page
text:
How to use it in your own page
Put the XML in your project, install the STACK SymPy and shared AI Feedback extensions, add filters: [stack-sympy] to _quarto.yml, and point a code block at one named question:
```{.stack-question}
#| file: questions/polynomial-expansion.xml
#| question: Expand a product (form-sensitive)
#| variants: 3
#| seed: 17
#| review: true
#| feedback: true
```
Render with quarto render, then serve the output over HTTP. The authoring guide explains the XML subset, diagnostics, grading, and the test command. The README has installation and development instructions.

title: Live browser UI review — question corpus
text:
Live browser UI review — question corpus
2026-10-15 · deployed commit 5c16adbc250e39f909639152c9d51ca3d701893c · Chrome cloud browser · verified URL https://erasmus-ctm.github.io/stack-sympy/corpus.html (also https://erasmus-ctm.github.io/stack-sympy/ and https://erasmus-ctm.github.io/stack-sympy/examples.html).
The deployed page loaded with 30 corpus table rows: 6 passed authored tests, 6 authored test mismatches, 11 unsupported at import, and 7 unsupported at instantiation. All 30 table question anchors resolved to existing document IDs, and all original XML hrefs pointed into the local questions/corpus/ path. The six passed entries alone displayed interactive cards. MathJax output was visible (mjx-container elements), with no diagnostic card. The desktop viewport was 1363 pixels wide and the document 1348 pixels wide, with no horizontal overflow. Visual screenshots of the overview, two-input card, expanded source controls, More examples feedback, and unsupported section showed readable typography and controls; the long copy prompt remained in its own scroll area.







Live interaction
Observed result




Follow table links to AlgMap-11.1, AlgMap-1.5, AlgMap-2.5
URLs acquired their respective fragments. The passed card showed labeled a and b inputs; mismatch showed seed/case, expected and produced score/answer note; import-blocked showed LowestTerms path/reason.


AlgMap-11.1 source disclosures
Both initially closed. Show source opened alone; Show STACK source opened independently and displayed original XML beginning with <?xml / <quiz><question type="stack">; both closed again. All six cards had both disclosures.


AlgMap-11.1 two inputs
Entered c/b and c/a; Validate displayed parsed previews, enabled Check; Check said “Correct.” Editing the first response to b/c cleared result and previews and disabled Check.


Six cards’ Run author tests
All reported authored tests passed on displayed seeds: AlgMap-1.6 2/2 (891319547), 7.1 2/2 (891379060), 9.1 1/1 (253453649), 9.6 1/1 (1775658430), 11.1 1/1 (17), 11.8 2/2 (17).


AlgMap-7.1 response form
Expanded x^2-64 validated and checked correctly. After editing to (x-8)*(x+8), stale result cleared and Check disabled; revalidating/checking showed “Not quite. Try again.”


Home Feedback
Empty response prompted “Enter an answer before requesting feedback.” With a response, default Copy prompt mode displayed Hint 1 and a prompt containing the response and implicit preceding section prose, with empty evidence. Settings displayed Copy prompt and Direct API modes and its data-sending disclosure; no credentials were entered or API called. Editing response removed old feedback and Check state; next request displayed Hint 2. Switching from variant 2 to 3 cleared answer/result, kept Check disabled, changed coefficients, and next request restarted at Hint 1.


More examples Feedback
Navigated from home to the deployed examples page. Five cards loaded. In three feedback-enabled cards, entered 1 and clicked Feedback in Copy prompt mode. Rational expression prompt included implicit section prose; three-field numeric prompt included explicit measurement-context and response entries for perimeter, area, and reported; imported STACK fixture prompt had no materials (context: none). All displayed Hint 1 with empty evidence/attachments; no API calls.



Browser-specific limitation: Clicking the corpus reproducible baseline JSON link produced a cloud browser policy rejection (“requested URL protocol is not allowed”; ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT). I stopped that navigation and did not retry or route around the restriction. Therefore this review verifies the baseline/manifest/license links’ presence and local hrefs, but not their direct opening/download in this browser. The primary agent independently verified the deployed gh-pages tree contains the baseline with 30 rows. Original XML direct download was likewise not claimed as browser-verified. This browser error is not evidence that the public files are missing. The unrelated cloud-browser telemetry errors concerning oaistatsig.com did not prevent these target-site interactions.
No product code was changed during this review. Detailed mathematical grading cases are in the companion corpus-live-math.md report.
